title: Signals of quality: failure detectors on every session, and feedback that becomes a person's correction
request: The owner wants the sessions worth reading found without reading them all, and wants their failures turned into benchmark cases. The morning when an anomaly-detection draft was built as a model of customer ids should be found by rule, by more than one detector.
spec: Nine detectors in dclab_core run on one visit's events, each with a session it must flag and sessions it must not: identifier_target, built_with_question_open, task_contradicts_words, rephrased, error, spend_without_result, build_refused_again, question_asked_again, left_unbuilt. The flags appear on the Sessions cards and the timeline. A feedback route records helpful, unhelpful or wrong on an answer, a proposal, a decision or a report, and "wrong" on a yes or no decision becomes a person's correction label.
plan: Detectors as pure rules over the shared event contract, so the main product can run the same ones on its own rows.
One read per visit, shared by the card and its flags.
Feedback as an event of kind feedback.given; on a yes or no decision, also a user_decision_exposed label saying the opposite.

decisions.decision: The data analysis's role for a column wins over its name.
decisions.why: country_code analysed as categorical is a category. A name is only a guess, so a hit on the name alone is medium severity, not high.

decisions.decision: Only blocking questions count for built_with_question_open, tracked per conversation.
decisions.why: Home lets a build go past the unit and action questions on purpose (dclab_core.card, blocks=False). An answer given in another conversation does not answer this one.

decisions.decision: A question asked again with different options is a follow-up, not a repeat.
decisions.why: Home asks for the outcome in words first, then asks again with the column options once the data arrives. That is the main flow, not a failure.

decisions.decision: Only someone who may change the work or review it turns "wrong" into a label, and only once.
decisions.why: A label weighs on what the decision models learn. A viewer's opinion is kept as feedback; duplicates would inflate the counts.

change: dclab_core/signals.py (new; 0.10.0), dclab_rnd/experience/__init__.py (visit_events, flags), experience/__main__.py, agentic/pages/sessions.py (flags and totals.flagged), agentic/pages/ledger.py (POST /api/feedback), accounts/guard.py, the Home feedback buttons, the Admin Sessions flags; tests/test_signals.py (new), test_experience_log.py; CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, the plan.

findings.defect: The camel-case key rule matched is_paid.
findings.scenario: A target is_paid was flagged as an identifier.
findings.cause: The case-insensitive key regex also read the camel-case suffixes, so 'id' at the end of 'paid' matched.
findings.fix: A separate case-sensitive regex for camelCase keys (customerId).

findings.defect: built_with_question_open treated every question as blocking.
findings.scenario: An action question, then a build, gave a high flag. So did an outcome question withdrawn by a label file, which has no answer from the person.
findings.cause: Every chat.agent question was treated as open; the blocks flag of dclab_core.card was ignored.
findings.fix: Count only BLOCKING fields, per conversation. Clear an open outcome question when the data is analysed: it is either withdrawn or asked again as a new question.

findings.defect: question_asked_again flagged Home's follow-up outcome question.
findings.scenario: The outcome given in words, then 'Which column records that outcome?' with column options, was flagged.
findings.cause: Any repeat of a field counted.
findings.fix: A repeat counts only with the same options, in the same conversation.

findings.defect: identifier_target flagged code columns at high severity, even against the analysis.
findings.scenario: country_code analysed as categorical, diagnosis_code and id_verified were all flagged.
findings.cause: The name rule included code and an id_ prefix, and it overrode the analysed role.
findings.fix: The role wins when the column was analysed. The name alone gives medium severity. code and the id_ prefix were dropped.

findings.defect: rephrased counted the same short answer to two different questions as a resend.
findings.scenario: 'Yes' to the labels question, then 'yes' to the action question.
findings.cause: Messages were compared across the whole visit.
findings.fix: Compare only messages since the agent's last question, per conversation.

findings.defect: spend_without_result flagged visits that only asked a question, and stages still running.
findings.scenario: A project question answered by its agent at a cost of 0.002 EUR.
findings.cause: Only a build and a finished stage counted as results.
findings.fix: An answer on the project or intern surface, a started stage or an export also counts as a result.

findings.defect: task_contradicts_words paired any draft's words with any saved solution, ignored edits, and missed anomaly built as binary.
findings.scenario: Two drafts in one visit, an edited problem, and 'nothing is labelled' saved as binary.
findings.cause: The draft and the saved solution were not matched, and binary was excluded for every family.
findings.fix: Match by conversation, or by the project the draft was built into, using the latest edit. Words that settle on anomaly flag any task.

findings.defect: A client-sent ref went into feedback.given.on, a meta field that every export keeps.
findings.scenario: ref set to an e-mail address.
findings.cause: The ref was cut to 80 characters but its shape was not checked.
findings.fix: Keep the ref only when it has an id's shape.

findings.defect: Any viewer could write a decision label. The label did not record who wrote it, and repeats added duplicates.
findings.cause: The route needs only read permission, and the label was written as person:feedback.
findings.fix: Write a label only for roles with write or review permission, as person:<user id>, once per person.

findings.defect: The must-not cases were mostly the one good session, far from the edge.
findings.scenario: None of the near misses in R1 to R6 was tested.
findings.fix: A list of everyday near misses per detector, plus the failures they must not hide.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each fix undone fails a test

measurements.name: the owner's morning
measurements.gate: flagged by at least two detectors
limits: A reconstruction of the morning's events, not the live log.

outcome: Every session now carries flags from nine rule-based detectors, written so that Home's normal flow raises none. Feedback joins the session record, and becomes a correction label only from someone entitled to correct.
lessons: A detector's must-not cases should be the product's everyday near misses, not the cleanest session.
A field marked meta leaves the workspace with every export: check a client-sent value's shape before putting it there.
risks: The card reads at most 5000 events a visit and the timeline 20000, so a very long visit's flags can differ between the two.
The detectors are rules: their precision on real sessions is not yet measured (19.12 turns flagged sessions into benchmark cases).
